title: Hull City announce arrests over discriminatory chants at FA Cup tie vs. Chelsea
content:
Hull City have announced that arrests have been made over discriminatory chanting during their fourth-round FA Cup tie against Chelsea on Friday.

A warning was sounded over the PA system to stop the chanting in the first half, after “Chelsea rent boy” was heard in the home crowd at the MKM Stadium.

The address reminded fans that discriminatory chanting is a criminal offence and that CCTV was being monitored inside the ground. In the second half a further announcement was made that action had been taken, including arrests made.

In January 2022, the Crown Prosecution Service confirmed that it considered the term “rent boy” a homophobic slur — and therefore a hate crime. This means anyone who uses it could be liable for prosecution under hate crime laws. The term originated in the 19th century and is a British slang for a male sex worker.

The home club had issued a warning on Thursday “to reaffirm that chanting of a homophobic, racist or discriminatory nature is entirely unacceptable and will not be tolerated”. The announcement, which came towards the end of the first half, also reminded supporters to report anything offensive they hear to a steward.

After the CPS confirmed the homophobic implications of the chant, Liverpool fan Paul Boardman was banned from entering Wembley Stadium for that year’s FA Cup final against Chelsea, having been heard shouting the term at a nearby station.

Boardman later pleaded guilty to using threatening words or behaviour to cause harassment, alarm or distress, contrary to Section 5 of the Public Order Act 1986. He was sentenced at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on December 5, 2022 and fined £500.
